headline: Right to Repair takes effect as ESPR and CSRD pressure mounts
summary: EU Right to Repair obligations have taken effect, placing direct liability on importers and brand owners of consumer equipment. Meanwhile, stakeholder pushback continues over proposed CSRD non-EU reporting reliefs, and ESPR focus increases on returned stock and product passports.

items.title: EU Right to Repair rules take effect alongside new consultation
items.what: The EU Right to Repair framework has taken effect, placing compliance obligations on importers, while the Commission launched a consultation on further repairability measures.
items.meaning: As the EU brand owner and importer of consumer power tools, legal responsibility for repair access and spare part availability rests with you.
items.action: Audit spare part logistics and update supply contracts with Chinese contract manufacturers.

sources.title: New Law on Right to Repair Takes Effect

items.title: ESPR implementation highlights circular return challenges and product passports
items.what: Industry reports highlight retail write-offs of returned goods under ESPR scrutiny, alongside early corporate implementations of Digital Product Passports.
items.meaning: Ecodesign rules will require greater product durability, waste prevention on returns, and digital trace data for tools and battery systems.
items.action: Review returned stock handling and align Chinese suppliers on Digital Product Passport data requirements.

sources.title: Half of retailers write off up to 40 per cent of returned stock, as ESPR raises pressure on circular returns

items.title: Pushback builds against proposed CSRD reliefs for non-EU firms
items.what: Investor and sustainable finance groups are opposing proposals to weaken CSRD reporting requirements for non-EU companies.
items.meaning: Your direct CSRD reporting starting in financial year 2027 remains firm, reinforcing the need for primary supply chain data from Chinese manufacturers.
items.action: Maintain supplier data collection programmes to ensure readiness for Scope 3 disclosures.
